conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I'm 55 years old, male. I've been having some right shoulder pain for a few weeks now. It started after doing some work in my backyard on a bunch of different projects, and it just hasn't gone away. It's been really sore, especially on the outside of my shoulder, and it hurts when I move it.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe the nature of the pain (e.g., sharp, dull, burning) and whether it radiates to other areas? Have you experienced any swelling, redness, or limited range of motion in the shoulder? Have you had any prior shoulder injuries or surgeries?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The pain is more of a soreness, kinda like a dull ache, and it's mostly on the outside of my shoulder. It doesn't really radiate anywhere else, but it definitely hurts when I move it, especially when I raise my arm. I have had some issues with that same shoulder before from playing baseball when I was younger, but nothing major. I don't remember any surgeries on it.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone any imaging studies or consultations for this shoulder pain, and if so, what were the findings or recommendations?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any imaging studies done for this yet, but my doctor mentioned looking at an X-ray and there was no fracture. They did say they might order an MRI since I've had some issues before. I'm not sure what exactly they're looking for, but I'm hoping it's nothing too serious.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any weakness, numbness, or tingling in your right arm or hand? Additionally, could you describe any specific activities or movements that aggravate or relieve the pain?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't experienced any weakness, numbness, or tingling in my right arm or hand. The pain is aggravated when I move my arm, especially when I raise it or do things like lift stuff, but it doesn't really bother me when I'm just sitting still. I've been trying to ice it and take some Advil, which helps a little, but it's still sore to touch.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you noticed any clicking, popping, or locking sensations in the shoulder when you move it?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't noticed any clicking, popping, or locking sensations in my shoulder when I move it. It just feels sore on the outside, especially when I raise my arm or do any lifting. It's been pretty consistent like that.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe the exact location of the pain on your shoulder and whether you have any difficulty performing daily activities such as dressing or reaching overhead?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The pain is on the outside of my shoulder, kind of near the top where the arm connects, and it's been bothering me when I try to reach overhead or do any lifting. It doesn't really stop me from doing daily stuff, but it does make some things a bit uncomfortable, like putting on a shirt or reaching for something high.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you had any recent imaging studies, such as an X-ray or MRI, of the right shoulder? If not, would you be willing to undergo an MRI to better evaluate the cause of your shoulder pain?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any recent imaging studies of the right shoulder yet. I was told they looked at an X-ray and there was no fracture, but they might order an MRI since I've had some issues before. I'm willing to do that if it helps figure out what's going on.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth around the affected shoulder area?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth around the affected shoulder area. It's just sore and tender on the outside, especially when I move it, but there's no visible inflammation or heat around it.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe the specific movements or activities that trigger the pain the most, and have you noticed any weakness or limited range of motion in your right shoulder?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The movements that trigger the pain the most are raising my arm or doing any kind of lifting, especially with the projects I've been working on in the yard. I don't really have any weakness, but I do feel some limitation when I try to move it a certain way, though I can still move it pretty well overall.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your arm or hand that could suggest nerve involvement?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in my arm or hand. It's just the soreness in the shoulder, and my hand grip feels fine. I don't think it's related to any nerve issues.

It started after I was doing a lot of work in the yard, but I don't remember specifically falling or hitting it. It just gradually started hurting after all the lifting and projects I've been doing.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: Yes, it does bother me a little at night because I sleep on that side, but it's not really keeping me up or disrupting my sleep too much. It's more of a mild discomfort that I notice when I shift positions.

conversation_turns.text: I'm 45 years old, male, and I'm here because of right elbow pain. I've been playing a lot of tennis lately, and it's been hurting for about three weeks.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please describe the nature of your elbow pain? For example, is it a sharp pain, a dull ache, or something else? Also, have you noticed any swelling, redness, or difficulty moving your elbow?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: It's a sharp, shooting pain, like it's stabbing. It's really bad when I use my elbow, even just reaching for something in the cupboard. I don't have any swelling or redness, but it's hard to move it without pain.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any previous injuries or surgeries involving your right elbow, or any history of repetitive strain or overuse in the upper extremities?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any injuries or surgeries on my right elbow, and I don't have a history of repetitive strain in my upper extremities other than the recent increase in tennis. I used to play a lot more back in high school, but that was a long time ago.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone any physical examination or imaging studies for your elbow pain, such as X-rays or an MRI?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any physical examination or imaging studies for my elbow pain yet. I just started feeling the pain a few weeks ago, so I haven't seen a doctor about it before today.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe the specific movements or activities that trigger the pain? For example, do you feel it more when you grip objects, lift things, or extend your arm?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The pain is really bad when I use my elbow, like when I try to grip something or lift things, and especially when I extend my arm. It feels like it's shooting and stabbing, and it's been getting worse the more I play tennis.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe the exact location of the pain in your right elbow? Is it on the inner (medial) or outer (lateral) side, or does it radiate to other areas?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The pain is on the outside part of my elbow, and it doesn't radiate anywhere else. It's really bad when I use my elbow, like when I try to grip something or lift things, and especially when I extend my arm. It feels like it's shooting and stabbing.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your hand or fingers associated with the elbow pain?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in my hand or fingers associated with the elbow pain. It's just the sharp, shooting pain on the outside of my elbow that makes it hard to use my arm without discomfort.

conversation_turns.text: Have you noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth around the affected elbow? Have you experienced any locking, clicking, or popping sensations during elbow movement?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient

conversation_turns.text: Have you had any prior imaging or physical examination of the right elbow? If so, what were the findings?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any prior imaging or physical examination of the right elbow. I just started feeling the pain a few weeks ago, so I haven't seen a doctor about it before today.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor

conversation_turns.text: I'm 27 years old and female. I've been feeling some really bad knee pain in my right knee, especially when I swim using the breaststroke. It started a few weeks ago, and it's been getting worse.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Can you describe the nature of the knee pain (e.g., sharp, dull, throbbing) and whether it is constant or only occurs during specific movements, such as during the breaststroke? Have you experienced any swelling, stiffness, or instability in the knee?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The pain feels like a dull ache, but it gets sharper when I move my knee a certain way, especially when I kick out my legs during the breaststroke. It doesn't happen all the time, just when I'm swimming, and I haven't noticed any swelling or instability, just pain when I do that movement.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Can you describe the specific movement during breaststroke that causes the sharp pain in your right knee? Have you noticed any patterns or triggers that make the pain worse?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The sharp pain happens when I kick my legs out like a frog during the breaststroke. It starts to hurt after I swim a couple of laps, and it feels worse the more I do it. I didn’t have any issues before I started swimming more regularly.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone any physical examination or imaging studies for your knee pain, such as an X-ray or MRI?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The doctor showed me the X-ray, and it was normal. He didn’t find any swelling, but there was pain when he moved my patella and when he had me stiffen my leg. He said it looks like chondromalacia of the patella, which is probably from overuse with swimming.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Thank you for sharing that information. To better understand your condition, could you describe the exact location of the pain on your knee and whether it radiates anywhere? Also, have you noticed any clicking, popping, or grinding sensations in the knee during or after swimming?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The pain is on the front of my right knee, around the patella area, and it doesn't really radiate anywhere else. I haven't noticed any clicking or popping, just the pain when I move my leg that way during the breaststroke.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you noticed any weakness in your quadriceps or any difficulty with straight leg raises? Have you had any prior episodes of patellar dislocation or subluxation?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't noticed any weakness in my quadriceps, and I can do straight leg raises without too much trouble. I don't think I've ever had any patellar dislocation or subluxation before.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please describe any other activities that might be causing or aggravating the knee pain, and have you noticed any improvement or worsening with rest or specific exercises?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I haven't noticed any other activities that cause the pain except for the breaststroke. The pain started after I began swimming more regularly, and it hasn't improved with rest. I haven't tried any specific exercises for it yet, but the doctor suggested straight leg raises to strengthen my quadriceps.

conversation_turns.text: I'm 32 years old, and I'm a female. I'm here because my IBS symptoms have been flaring up again, with abdominal pain, nausea, and some vomiting. It's been worse since I've been eating out more often, especially on weekends.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe the nature and location of your abdominal pain, as well as the frequency and characteristics of your nausea and vomiting?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The abdominal pain is a cramping and sharp pain, mostly in my lower belly, and it comes and goes. The nausea happens more when I eat out, especially after spicy or fatty foods, and I've been vomiting occasionally, but not too often. It's been worse since I started going to Friday nights and Saturday nights out.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you had any prior episodes of IBS flare-ups, and if so, what was the pattern or triggers for those episodes? Additionally, have you been diagnosed with any other gastrointestinal conditions or allergies in the past?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I've had IBS flare-ups before, especially around the same time last year when I was seen in August 2019. The triggers seem to be similar—eating out, spicy or fatty foods, and drinking alcohol, especially on weekends. I don't recall having any other gastrointestinal conditions or allergies, but I was prescribed Reglan before, which I used as needed for nausea.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you share any details about your family history of gastrointestinal disorders, as well as any physical symptoms you've noticed recently, such as abdominal tenderness, bowel sounds, or signs of dehydration?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I don't have any family history of gastrointestinal disorders that I'm aware of. Recently, I haven't had any tenderness in my abdomen, and my bowel sounds seem normal. I haven't noticed any signs of dehydration, but I have been drinking more water instead of sodas, which I think has helped a little.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you had any recent stool tests, blood tests, or imaging studies to evaluate your current symptoms?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any recent stool tests, blood tests, or imaging studies for my current symptoms. I was last seen in August 2019, and since then, I've been managing my symptoms with medications like Bentyl and Zofran as needed. My doctor hasn't ordered any new tests recently.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you clarify if there is any family history of gastrointestinal disorders, such as IBS, Crohn's disease, or ulcerative colitis, that you are aware of?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I don't have any family history of gastrointestinal disorders like IBS, Crohn's disease, or ulcerative colitis that I'm aware of.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as increased frequency, diarrhea, constipation, or alternating patterns, since the flare-up began?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: Yes, my bowel habits have changed a bit since the flare-up began. I'm having two to three bowel movements a day, and they're usually formed stools. However, after eating out or drinking, I tend to have more diarrhea. It's been inconsistent, but it's definitely more frequent than usual.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any weight loss, rectal bleeding, or persistent fever during this flare-up?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't experienced any weight loss, rectal bleeding, or persistent fever during this flare-up. I've been managing the symptoms with medication and trying to adjust my diet and alcohol intake. I feel like I'm handling it better than before, but it's still uncomfortable at times.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe the frequency and severity of your abdominal pain, and what specific types of foods seem to trigger your symptoms the most?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The abdominal pain happens pretty often, especially after I eat out or drink alcohol. It's usually cramping or sharp pains in my lower belly, and it feels worse after I eat spicy or fatty foods, like the alfredo sauce at the restaurant. I've noticed that fried chicken doesn't bother me as much, but I still try to watch my portions.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you had any recent changes in your medication regimen, such as starting or stopping any medications, or adjusting the dosage of Bentyl or Zofran?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't made any recent changes to my medication regimen. I've been using Bentyl as needed for cramping and Zofran for nausea, just like before. I haven't stopped or started anything new, but I did mention that I haven't been consistent with the Citrucel fiber supplement. I think I need to find a better way to take it regularly.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you had any recent stool tests, blood tests, or imaging studies to evaluate your current symptoms?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any recent stool tests, blood tests, or imaging studies to evaluate my current symptoms. so.subjective:
* The patient is a 72-year-old woman who is seeking a follow-up on her hypertension and is interested in discussing a shot for managing her drinking.
* She was diagnosed with hypertension a while back and is currently taking hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg once daily and half a dose of lisinopril 20 mg due to side effects from the full dose.
* The patient reports that they feel more confident in their ability to achieve the desired outcome with the injectable form of naltrexone compared to the pill form.
* The patient reports that they do not have specific triggers for their alcohol use, but they find it difficult to stop on their own.
* The patient reports that their blood pressure readings at home decrease slightly when they sit for a while before taking them.
* She has been checking her blood pressure at home and reports fluctuations, with higher readings in the evenings and lower readings in the mornings.
* The patient reports that their blood pressure readings tend to be higher in the evenings, with values reaching up to 150 over 100.
* She has been drinking hard alcohol four to five times a week for a long time and has tried to cut back on her own but struggles with the urge to drink.
* The patient reports that she prefers the injectable form of naltrexone over the pill form because it cannot be easily reversed.
* She is interested in the shot (naltrexone/Vivitrol) to help her with her drinking and has previously taken the pill form but did not stick with it due to missing doses.
* The patient denies having liver disease or other contraindications to naltrexone/Vivitrol.

conversation_turns.text: I'm 72 years old, and I'm a woman. I'm here for a follow-up on my hypertension, and I also wanted to talk about the shot you mentioned last time for helping with my drinking.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you clarify what you meant by 'the shot' for managing your drinking? Additionally, could you provide more details about your hypertension, such as when you were diagnosed and any medications you are currently taking?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The shot is for helping me stop drinking, something we talked about last time. As for my hypertension, I was diagnosed a while back, and I'm currently taking hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg once daily and half a dose of lisinopril 20 mg, because when I first took the full dose, I felt really tired and had some headaches and a swooshing sound in my left ear. I've been checking my blood pressure at home, and it's been fluctuating, usually higher in the evenings but lower in the mornings.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you provide more details about your blood pressure readings, including the specific values you've been recording at home and the time of day they were taken?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: Sure. In the mornings, my blood pressure is generally lower, around 130 to 145 over 95 to 100. But in the evenings, it tends to be higher, sometimes up to 150 over 100. I noticed that if I sit for a while before taking it, it goes down a bit, like when I come in here for my appointment. I take my medications in the morning, which is why my morning numbers seem more normal.

conversation_turns.text: I'm 52 years old, and I'm here because I've been having a lot of pain on the inside of my right elbow. It's been hurting for about four days now, and it's really bad—it's a seven out of ten. It even wakes me up at night, and it's making it hard for me to work on my pottery, which I've been really into lately.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please confirm your age, gender, and describe the nature of the pain in your right elbow, including any activities that aggravate or relieve it?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: Sure, I'm 52 years old, and I'm a woman. The pain is on the inside of my right elbow, and it hurts when I try to do things like bend my wrist or use my arm for pottery. It doesn't really get better with anything I've tried, like ice or ibuprofen, and it's been getting me up at night.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any recent trauma or injury to your right elbow, or do you have a history of repetitive use or occupational strain on that arm?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I don't think I've hit my elbow on anything, and I don't have a history of injury there. But I have been doing a lot of pottery lately, which involves using my arm a lot, and I think that's probably what's causing the pain.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any swelling, redness, or stiffness in the affected elbow? Have you noticed any numbness or tingling in your hand or fingers?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't noticed any swelling, redness, or stiffness in my elbow, and I don't have any numbness or tingling in my hand or fingers. It's just the pain on the inside of my elbow that's been really bothering me.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any recent trauma or repetitive strain to the right elbow, and have you noticed any radiation of pain to your forearm or hand?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I don't think I've had any recent trauma to my elbow, but I have been doing a lot of pottery, which involves repetitive motions. The pain does radiate down my arm, along the inside of it, but I haven't felt anything in my hand or fingers.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any clicking, locking, or popping sensations in your right elbow during the pain episodes?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't felt any clicking, locking, or popping in my elbow during the pain episodes. It's just the constant ache on the inside that's been really bothering me, especially at night.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any weakness in your grip or difficulty lifting objects with your right hand?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't noticed any weakness in my grip or difficulty lifting objects with my right hand. I can still manage everyday tasks, but it's really hard to work on my pottery because of the pain. It's been so bad that it's keeping me up at night.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any previous episodes of elbow pain or been diagnosed with any musculoskeletal or autoimmune conditions in the past?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I don't think I've had any previous episodes of elbow pain, and I don't have any musculoskeletal or autoimmune conditions that I'm aware of. This is the first time I've experienced pain like this in my elbow.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone any imaging studies such as X-rays or MRI of the right elbow in the past, and if so, what were the findings?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient

conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your hand or fingers, especially on the side of your little finger and ring finger, which could suggest ulnar nerve involvement?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in my hand or fingers, especially on the side of my little finger and ring finger. I just have this constant ache on the inside of my elbow that radiates down my arm, but my hand and fingers feel normal.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe any specific movements or activities related to your pottery work that seem to make the pain worse?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: Well, I've been using my right arm a lot on the pottery wheel, especially when I'm shaping the clay and trying to get the bowl just right. It's the repetitive motion of turning the wheel and pressing into the clay that seems to make it worse. I think that's been putting a lot of strain on my elbow.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth around your right elbow, or any stiffness in the joint that makes it difficult to move your arm?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any recent changes in the strength of your right hand or fingers, or any difficulty performing fine motor tasks with your right hand?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I'm 58 years old and female. I'm here because I have this foot ulcer that just won't heal, and I'm worried about it. It's been going on for about a year now.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please provide more details about your diabetes status, including whether you have been diagnosed with diabetes, the type of diabetes, and how long you have had it? Additionally, have you had any history of infections or cardiovascular conditions?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I was diagnosed with type two diabetes a few years back, and my blood sugars have been running in the two hundreds, which my doctor doesn't like. My last A1C was about ten, so I know it's not well-controlled. I haven't had any major infections or heart issues that I'm aware of.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe the location, size, appearance, and any associated symptoms (e.g., pain, drainage, odor) of the foot ulcer? Have you noticed any changes in its appearance over the past year?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: It's on the top of my right foot, near the fifth toe, and it's about an inch in size. It's got some yellow stuff in it, and there's been more drainage lately. It doesn't hurt, but I don't feel much in my foot anyway. I've noticed it hasn't been getting better, and it seems to be getting more draining over time.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you had any recent fever, chills, or signs of systemic infection such as malaise or weight loss? Have you had any prior wound cultures or imaging of the foot ulcer?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I haven't had any fever or chills, but I have been feeling more tired lately. As for imaging, I think they did an x-ray before I came in, and it showed no bone infection, if I remember right. I don't think they did a wound culture.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please describe the depth of the ulcer and whether there is any necrotic tissue present? Additionally, have you noticed any changes in the color or texture of the surrounding skin?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The ulcer isn't very deep as far as I can tell, and there's some yellow stuff in there, but I don't think there's any dead tissue exposed. The skin around it doesn't look red or swollen, and it doesn't feel different to the touch. It just looks kind of open and has that yellowish stuff in it.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Has the patient had any prior episodes of foot ulcers or infections, and is she currently on any antibiotics or wound care regimen?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I don't think I've had any other foot ulcers before, just this one. I was on some antibiotics a while back, maybe five months ago, but I don't think I'm on anything now. I've been trying to take care of it, but nothing really seems to be working.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Has the patient undergone any vascular studies, such as an ankle-brachial index (ABI) or Doppler ultrasound, to assess peripheral arterial disease?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I don't think I've had any vascular studies done before. I wasn't really aware that was something they would check for this kind of wound. I just thought it was a regular ulcer that wasn't healing.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please share more details about your current diabetes management, including any medications you are taking, your diet, and whether you have experienced any complications related to your diabetes?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: My diabetes is still not great, my blood sugars are still running around two hundred, and my last A1c was about ten. I'm on insulin and metformin, but it's not where my doctor wants it to be. I try to eat better, but I know I'm not doing enough. I also don't take good care of my feet like I should, which is probably making this ulcer worse.

conversation_turns.text: Has the patient experienced any new or worsening symptoms since discontinuing Crestor, such as chest pain, shortness of breath, or fatigue?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I'm 82 years old, and I'm a male. I'm here because I had an acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation, and I was in the hospital for a few days. I felt really bad with shortness of breath and swelling in my ankles, and I even had to call 911. But now I feel much better.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please provide more details about your current symptoms and how long you've been experiencing them?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: Sure, doc. The swelling in my ankles has been going on for a while, but it got worse before I went to the hospital. And the shortness of breath came on pretty suddenly—one day I was fine, and the next I was struggling to breathe. I had to call 911, and they gave me that special mask to help me breathe. But since I've been home, I haven't had any trouble breathing or swelling anymore. I feel good now.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please provide details about any prior heart failure diagnoses, medications you were taking during your hospitalization, and any previous hospitalizations related to heart failure or other conditions?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I was told I have chronic kidney disease and hypertension, and this was the first time I had an acute heart failure episode. During the hospital stay, they gave me some medications, including a water pill that made me go to the bathroom a lot, and some blood pressure meds. I don't remember the exact names, but I'm taking them now as prescribed. I haven't been hospitalized for heart failure before, but I have had some issues with my kidneys.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please provide the specific names and dosages of the medications you are currently taking, including the diuretic and blood pressure medications?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I'm taking Bumex, which is the water pill, and I think it's two milligrams once a day. For my blood pressure, I'm on Cozaar and Norvasc, but I don't remember the exact dosages. The doctor told me to keep taking them, so I do.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you provide the results of any recent blood tests, such as serum creatinine, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and electrolyte levels, as well as any imaging studies like an echocardiogram or renal ultrasound that were performed during or after the hospitalization?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I was told that I have chronic kidney disease and that my echocardiogram showed a preserved ejection fraction of 55%, abnormal diastolic filling, and mild to moderate mitral regurgitation. The doctor also mentioned ordering a renal artery ultrasound to check for any secondary causes affecting my kidneys, but I haven’t had the results yet.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please provide your current serum creatinine level, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and electrolyte levels (such as sodium, potassium, and bicarbonate)? This information will help us better understand your kidney function and guide your care.

conversation_turns.text: Can you describe the exact location of the knee pain? Is it on one side or both sides of the knee? Have you experienced any swelling, stiffness, or locking of the knee? Have you had any prior injuries or surgeries to the knee?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The pain is behind my kneecaps, and it's on both sides. I haven't had any swelling or stiffness, and my knee doesn't lock up. I don't remember ever injuring my knees before, just that one time I broke my arm in sixth grade.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone any imaging studies or blood tests for your knee pain? If so, could you share the results?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I don't remember having any imaging studies or blood tests done specifically for my knee pain. My primary care doctor referred me to you, so I guess this is the first time I'm being evaluated for it.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you provide details about your current activity level, occupation, and any recent changes in physical activity that might be contributing to your knee pain?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I work from home, so I'm at my desk a lot, and I used to run about five to six miles a day. Now, I can barely get to half a mile before my knee starts hurting. I try to stay as active as I can, but it's been really tough lately.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please provide information about any family history of joint-related conditions, such as rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, or lupus?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I don't have any information about my family history regarding joint-related conditions. I don't think that's something we've discussed before.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any morning stiffness, fatigue, or systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss that could suggest an inflammatory or autoimmune condition?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't experienced any morning stiffness, fatigue, fever, or weight loss. The pain is pretty much just in my knees and doesn't seem to be connected to anything else in my body.

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The pain gets worse when I get up from a seated position, after watching TV, or when going up and down stairs. It does feel better when I rest for a while, but it's really hard to do anything without it hurting now.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you noticed any clicking, popping, or grinding sensations in your knees during movement?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: Yes, sometimes I can hear what sounds like creaking in my knees, especially when I move them a certain way. It's kind of unsettling, but I didn't think to mention it until now.

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I'm 57 years old, male. I've been having some joint pain in both knees, especially in the last few days. They feel stiff and sore when I wake up, and it kind of lingers throughout the day. I've been riding my bike more lately, and I think that might be contributing to it.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please confirm your age, gender, and the duration of your knee pain? Also, could you describe the nature of the pain and any activities that make it better or worse?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I'm 57, male. The knee pain has been going on for about three to four days. It's been getting worse, especially in the mornings when I wake up—they feel really stiff and sore. By the end of the day, the pain lingers, and it's kind of like that same soreness I feel around dinner time. I've been riding my bike more, and I think that's probably making it worse.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you had any prior joint issues, autoimmune conditions, or injuries? Also, could you describe the type of knee pain you're experiencing—sharp, dull, or throbbing—and whether there is any swelling, redness, or warmth in the affected areas? Lastly, do you have a family history of joint-related conditions?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I don't have any prior joint issues or injuries, and I don't recall any family history of joint-related conditions. As for the type of pain, it's more of a soreness and stiffness, especially in the mornings. There's some swelling and redness, but it's not too bad, and it seems to be a little less noticeable by the afternoon.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please describe if there is any warmth or tenderness in your knees, and have you noticed any locking or clicking sensations while moving your knees?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: There's a little tenderness in my knees, especially in the right one, and it does hurt a bit when I press on it. I haven't noticed any locking or clicking when I move them, just the soreness and stiffness.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone any recent blood tests or imaging studies for your knee pain, such as X-rays, MRI, or blood work for inflammatory markers?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any recent blood tests or imaging studies for my knee pain. I just started noticing the pain a few days ago, and I haven't seen a doctor about it before today.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any systemic symptoms such as fever, fatigue, or weight loss in conjunction with the knee pain?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't experienced any fever, fatigue, or weight loss with the knee pain. It's just been the stiffness and soreness in my knees, especially in the mornings.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any previous episodes of knee pain or injury, and if so, what was the nature and outcome of those episodes?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I don't recall any previous episodes of knee pain or injury. This is the first time I've experienced this kind of pain, and it started a few days ago. I haven't had any injuries to my knees, just the soreness and stiffness that's been getting worse.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you noticed any locking, clicking, or instability in your knees?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't noticed any locking, clicking, or instability in my knees. It's just been the soreness and stiffness, especially in the mornings. The pain is there, but it doesn't feel like my knees are giving out or making any strange noises when I move them.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you noticed any morning stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes, or any swelling that worsens with activity? Have you had any recent infections or illnesses?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, the stiffness doesn't last more than 30 minutes, and the swelling is more noticeable in the morning but doesn't really get worse with activity. I haven't had any recent infections or illnesses, just this knee pain and stiffness.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone any blood tests or imaging studies for your knees in the past, even if not recently? If so, what were the results?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I don't think I've had any blood tests or imaging studies for my knees in the past. I haven't had any issues with my knees before this, so I didn't think to get anything done. This is the first time I've had this kind of pain.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you noticed any specific activities or times of day when the pain worsens, and have you experienced any similar symptoms in other joints?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, the pain doesn't seem to be worse during specific activities, except maybe when I'm riding my bike, which I've been doing more of lately. And no, I haven't had any similar symptoms in other joints—just the knees.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth in your knees, and does the pain improve or worsen with rest?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't experienced any fever, fatigue, or weight loss with the knee pain. It's just been the soreness and stiffness, especially in the mornings. The pain is there, but it doesn't feel like my knees are giving out or making any strange noises when I move them.

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any recent blood tests like a CBC, ESR, or CRP. I didn't think to get them because I didn't realize the knee pain could be related to something more than just overuse from biking. I just assumed it was from working out more.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor

conversation_turns.text: Yes, I had back surgery in November of 2020. It was a microdiscectomy because my disk broke off and wrapped around my spinal thecal sac. It was a pretty horrible experience, but at least it wasn't the poop sac. I had a lot of nerve pain down my leg and in my back, and I was on a high dose of gabapentin for it. It was tough to get off of.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you confirm your exact age and gender, and describe the nature of the pain in your right knee? Have you noticed any swelling, stiffness, or difficulty bearing weight on it?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I'm female, and I'm 38 years old. The pain is a constant ache, especially when I walk or go up hills. It doesn't really swell, but it feels unstable sometimes, like it might shift when I'm walking. It's hard to put weight on it without it hurting.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone any imaging or medical evaluations for your knee injury since the fall?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: Yes, I had x-rays done today, and the doctor looked at them. He said the x-rays looked pretty normal, but he still thinks I might have injured my posterior cruciate ligament. He wants me to get an MRI to check for any other issues like a meniscus tear or cartilage damage.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any locking, catching, or giving way of the knee since the injury?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't experienced any locking or catching, but sometimes it feels like it shifts when I walk, which is pretty unsettling. It doesn't really give way completely, but it's not stable either.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe the specific location of the pain in your right knee and whether it radiates to other areas?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The pain is on the inside of my right knee, right along the medial joint line. It doesn't really radiate anywhere else, just stays right there. It's pretty tender when touched, and it hurts more when I walk up hills or put weight on it.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe any specific movements or activities that make the pain worse or better? Have you noticed any locking, clicking, or popping sensations in the knee?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The pain gets worse when I walk up hills or put weight on it, and it's especially tender on the inside of my knee. I haven't noticed any locking or popping, but sometimes it feels like it shifts when I'm walking, which is pretty unsettling.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone any ligament testing, such as Lachman's test, anterior drawer test, or posterior drawer test, to assess the stability of your knee?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The doctor did do some testing on my knee. He checked the ligaments and said the medial collateral ligament is intact, and there's a little laxity in the posterior drawer. He compared it to my other knee and said it feels a bit unstable, but nothing too severe. He didn't do the Lachman test specifically, but he did mention that the anterior drawer was negative.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Thank you for sharing that information. To better understand your condition, could you tell me if you've noticed any locking or catching sensations in your knee, or if there are specific activities that make the pain worse?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I haven't noticed any locking or catching sensations in my knee, but the pain definitely gets worse when I walk up hills or put weight on it. It's especially tender on the inside of my knee, and sometimes it feels like it shifts when I'm walking, which is pretty unsettling.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Has the patient undergone any previous imaging studies for the knee, such as an MRI or ultrasound, prior to this incident?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any imaging studies done for my knee before this incident. The doctor did take some x-rays today, and they looked pretty normal, but he thinks I might need an MRI to get a better look at what's going on inside the knee.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Thank you for confirming that you haven't had any prior imaging for your knee. Since the X-rays were normal, the next step is to proceed with an MRI to evaluate for possible meniscus tear or cartilage damage. Is there anything else you'd like to share about your symptoms or concerns before we move forward with the MRI?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I don't think there's anything else to share right now. The main thing is that I want to get better and get back to walking my dog and doing my job without pain. I just hope it doesn't require surgery.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Thank you for sharing your concerns, Beverly. I understand how important it is for you to get back to your daily activities without pain. conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I don't think there's anything else to share right now. The main thing is that I want to get better and get back to walking my dog and doing my job without pain. I just hope it doesn't require surgery.

conversation_turns.text: Thank you for sharing your concerns. I understand how important it is for you to get back to your daily activities without pain. conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Thank you for the details. Could you please describe the exact nature of the shifting sensation you feel in your knee when walking? conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The shifting sensation feels like the knee is kind of sliding or moving a little to the side when I walk, and it's not super obvious, but it's enough to make me feel unstable. I can still straighten and bend it all the way, but sometimes it clicks when I do, and it feels a little weak when I'm going up hills.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please describe how often you experience the shifting sensation in your knee and whether it occurs during specific activities? Also, have you noticed any locking or catching in your knee, even if it's not frequent?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The shifting sensation happens pretty often when I'm walking, especially on uneven ground or when I'm turning. It doesn't happen all the time, but it's enough to make me feel like the knee isn't stable. I haven't noticed any locking or catching, just that odd sliding feeling and the clicking sometimes.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe the nature of the clicking sensation in your knee when you bend or straighten it? Is it a sharp click, a soft snap, or something else? conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The clicking is more like a soft snap when I bend or straighten it, not really sharp. And I can still bend and straighten it all the way, but sometimes it feels a little stiff, especially in the morning.
